title: EFC-C v2.1: Degree-Heterogeneity Entropy-Gradient Predictions for Cognitive States
description: Revises EFC-C by replacing the λ2 (Fiedler) formulation with a degree-heterogeneity bridge (B1**) linking hub-to-periphery degree ratio to the centrifugal entropy score. Introduces a two-layer prediction scheme: Layer A (topological, parameter-light) tests a power-law scaling with exponent γ≈0.55; Layer B (absolute-scale) tests a cross-domain-anchored constant Ceff fixed a priori via regime transformation of C=k/aG.
abstract: This revision of EFC-C replaces the Fiedler-eigenvalue formulation (Bridge B1*) used in v2.0 with the empirically-supported degree-heterogeneity formulation (Bridge B1**). The centrifugal entropy score κ = ⟨S_hub⟩/⟨S_periph⟩ is predicted from the structural hub-to-periphery degree ratio D_ratio = ⟨k_hub⟩/⟨k_periph⟩ via the power-law relation κ = C_eff · D_ratio^γ, where C_eff is fixed prior to neural data analysis via regime transformation of the cosmological constant C = k/a_G, and γ ≈ 0.55 is the one empirical fit parameter (constrained to 0.5 ≤ γ ≤ 0.6 across HCP datasets). Predictions are separated into Layer A (topological: invariant under cross-domain anchor C_eff) and Layer B (absolute scale: conditional on C_eff).

kappa_def.description: Centrifugal entropy score: ratio of mean multiscale entropy between hub and peripheral parcels.

Dratio_def.description: Hub-to-periphery degree ratio computed from weighted structural connectivity (top 10% hubs, bottom 30% periphery).

kappa_powerlaw.description: Bridge B1** prediction: entropy-gradient magnitude scales as a power law of structural degree heterogeneity with exponent \gamma (empirical, ~0.55).

Ceff_def.description: Effective cross-domain constant fixed a priori by regime transformation (RCMP) of the cosmological constant C=k/a_G into the cognitive regime.

alpha_AP.description: Anterior-posterior entropy asymmetry; discriminates schizophrenia (anterior-elevated) from MDD (posterior-shifted).

C_eff.source: Regime-transformed from cosmological C = k/a_G via RCMP L3→L1 factor (Bridge paper Sec 2.3); fixed prior to neural analysis

gamma.source: Empirical fit, estimated once from HCP reference sample

D_ratio_baseline.source: Typical HCP value, top 10% / bottom 30% partition with log-degree proxy

kappa_healthy_central.source: Layer B prediction with propagated EBE-bounded uncertainty

kappa_crit.description: Critical threshold at degree hierarchy collapse

key_results.main_finding: Framework update: κ is predicted by a one-parameter power law in hub–periphery degree heterogeneity (γ≈0.55), with absolute scale anchored by a preregistered Ceff; predictions are layered to separate topology-only tests (Layer A) from cross-domain absolute-scale tests (Layer B).

predictions.description: Layer A (topological): Δ log κ = γ · Δ log D_ratio with slope γ ∈ [0.5, 0.6]
predictions.observable: Log-log slope from regression of κ on D_ratio across pooled subjects
predictions.falsification: Fitted γ outside [0.3, 0.8] (±2σ EBE-bounded) for n ≥ 30, or Pearson r(log κ, log D_ratio) < 0.50

predictions.description: α_AP^scz > α_AP^healthy (anterior-dominant entropy elevation in schizophrenia)
κ_crit ≲ 1.9 at D_ratio ≲ 0.9 (degree hierarchy collapse, convergence κ → 1)

sealed_predictions.statement: Layer A (topological): Across subjects, log κ scales linearly with log Dratio with slope γ in [0.50, 0.60] using the preregistered hub/periphery partition and MSE-based κ.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: If the fitted γ falls outside [0.50, 0.60] or the κ–Dratio association is weak/non-significant across independent cohorts using the preregistered pipeline.

sealed_predictions.statement: Layer B (absolute scale): With Ceff fixed a priori via RCMP, the predicted κ = Ceff·Dratio^γ matches observed κ at the group and individual levels (after the specified τc secondary correction) without re-fitting Ceff.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: If fixing Ceff a priori leads to systematic, large absolute-scale mismatches that cannot be remedied by the preregistered τc correction.

sealed_predictions.statement: Degree heterogeneity Dratio explains substantially more inter-subject variance in κ than algebraic connectivity λ2 under the same preprocessing and partitioning.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: If λ2 explains equal or greater variance in κ than Dratio across datasets using identical pipelines and QC.

kill_criteria: KC1 (Layer A kill): In two or more independent, high-quality datasets (e.g., HCP and one OpenNeuro cohort), the fitted log–log slope between κ and Dratio lies outside the preregistered interval γ ∈ [0.50, 0.60] using the specified hub (top 10%) and periphery (bottom 30%) partitions and MSE-based κ.

KC2 (Layer A kill): After preregistered QC and nuisance controls, Dratio fails to show a significant association with κ (e.g., non-significant slope or r^2 near zero) in at least two independent datasets, while analyses follow the specified pipeline.

KC3 (Model driver kill): Under identical pipelines, λ2 (algebraic connectivity) consistently explains more variance in κ than Dratio (e.g., adjusted R^2(λ2) > adjusted R^2(Dratio) by a meaningful margin) across independent datasets.

KC4 (Partition robustness kill): The κ–Dratio scaling collapses (slope or significance lost) across reasonable, preregistered variations of the hub/periphery thresholds (e.g., hubs 5–15%, periphery 20–40%), indicating dependence on an idiosyncratic partition.

KC5 (Layer B kill): With Ceff fixed a priori via the RCMP mapping (no re-fitting on neural data), absolute-scale predictions show large, systematic bias across cohorts that cannot be resolved by the specified τc secondary correction (i.e., Layer B fails while Layer A holds).

KC6 (Transfer invalidation): Independent calibration attempts demonstrate that Ceff must be re-fit on neural data to achieve adequate absolute-scale performance, contradicting the preregistered cross-domain transfer claim (this kills the cross-domain anchor while leaving Layer A testable).

related_packages.role: Defines Bridge B1** (degree-heterogeneity formulation) and RCMP regime transformation used to fix Ceff.
Empirical support that local degree heterogeneity predicts functional variability/entropy gradients (r^2≈0.94).
Source of cosmological constant C=k/aG used in regime transformation to obtain Ceff.
EBE framework for layer-separated, validity-bounded inference.
Regime-Consistent Measurement Principle: methodological foundation for L3→L1 transfer of C_eff.
